statusText: The US cash open produced continuation rather than retracement: NQ is printing at its session high and the NDX day low is still the opening print, with yields, VIX, oil, semiconductors and megacaps all aligned behind the advance. Observed one-way structure lifts Tail into the elevated band; mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES.
recommendation: A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 14:00Z to 17:00Z, covering the observed opening continuation leg through the European close. Directional efficiency is currently high enough that mean reversion is unreliable within that window. The forecast has conditional Tail easing back to the watch band from 16:00Z and beneath it after the 20:00Z cash close, and the horizon contains no strong-block or off state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 prints session highs through the first cash hour as oil slides a fourth day, yields ease and chip stocks lead
body:
NQ futures traded 30,463.00 (+1.82%, +545.75) as of 14:16Z, printing at the 30,463.75 session high after a continuous advance from the 29,904.00 European low. The NDX cash index was 30,203.15 (+1.89%) at 14:26Z against a 29,933.22-30,207.30 range, so the session low is still the opening print and the first cash hour has produced no meaningful retracement. Friday's NDX close was 29,644.17.

Cross-asset confirmation is broad. The curve is lower across maturities, with the 2-year near 4.74%, the 5-year 4.83%, the 10-year 4.97% and the 30-year 5.30%. WTI is down 4.70% to roughly $95.59 and Brent down 3.72% to roughly $100.01, a fourth consecutive decline attributed to diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the US-Iran conflict and to reports that Strait of Hormuz flows have proved resilient. VIX is 14.72, at the bottom of a 14.72-14.99 range, so there is no volatility bid behind the equity advance.

The catalyst stack is one-sided and supportive. Treasury Secretary Bessent described preliminary weekend talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng as successful and proposed a US-China AI dialogue, ahead of a scheduled Trump-Xi summit on Thursday. The PHLX Semiconductor index has climbed more than 2% to its highest since September 9, and Meta has risen sharply ahead of its Connect event later this week. Today's US calendar is light: the Chicago Fed National Activity Index has already printed at -0.04 and only the 15:30Z bill auctions remain.

The risk assessment is driven by price path rather than by headlines. An index at its session extreme roughly one hour into the cash session, with the day low equal to the open and every major cross-asset aligned, is the observed persistent-directional-efficiency case in which mean reversion is denied for long enough to matter. That combination moves Tail from the watch band into the elevated band and maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Two features cap the escalation rather than extending it: VIX is at its session low, which describes an orderly grind rather than violent repricing, and there is no scheduled Tier-1 US catalyst today that could supply a delayed second leg. The elevated window is therefore drawn narrowly, from 14:00Z to 17:00Z, and conditional Tail decays through the US afternoon and evening. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours document a regime change rather than a steady state. Through Sunday's futures session and the Asian hours conditions were quiet and range-consistent, with Tail between 5 and 9 and mode normal. From roughly 06:00Z a steady bid built on the oil retreat and constructive US-China headlines: mode turned trend-up and Tail ratcheted from 5 to 22 across eight hourly assessments, crossing into the watch band at 11:00Z, while confidence improved from 81 to 86 as live evidence accumulated. Twenty-one of the 24 hours carried a mapped EA_ON state and none reached the block threshold; the escalation into the elevated band happens in the current hour, at the cash open, not in the lookback.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the elevated band for the observed continuation leg through 15:30Z, steps back into the watch band from 16:00Z as European liquidity withdraws, eases through the US afternoon with a small structural power-hour uptick, and falls beneath the watch band after the 20:00Z cash close. The overnight path settles into the quiet range baseline that the lookback shows is typical, then drifts up modestly with Tuesday's European liquidity and again into Tuesday's pre-open. The horizon contains no strong-block or off state at any hour. The current elevated reading rests on observed structure - price at the session extreme with the day low equal to the open - so it should decay quickly if a genuine retracement appears; every later hour frames structure conditionally because no post-15:00Z price path has been observed. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the current evidence set. Wednesday's flash PMIs and Thursday's scheduled Trump-Xi summit are the next regime-relevant catalysts.
